target.title: fix(line): use precise control-command check for group mention bypass
target.body:
Closes #107225

## What Problem This Solves

In a LINE group with `requireMention: true` (the default), an allowlisted member's ordinary message that just happens to contain an inline slash/bang token — `cd /home`, `go to /settings`, `!nice` — bypasses the mention requirement and gets dispatched to the agent, even though nobody @mentioned the bot. The bot pipes up on plain chatter. Only a real control command (or an actual @mention) should bypass `requireMention`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The group mention-bypass in `src/channels/mention-gating.ts` gates on `command.hasControlCommand`. LINE fed that field the broad `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` detector, whose `hasInlineCommandTokens` returns true for any `(?:^|\s)[/!][a-z]` token. That detector's job is deciding whether to *compute* CommandAuthorized metadata — per its own comment, it "errs on the side of false positives … not normal chat replies" — not whether a message *is* a control command. Using it for the bypass lets normal chat replies through the gate.

The fix routes the group path through the precise `hasControlCommand` (message starts with a configured command alias) and keeps the broad detector for DMs, which have no mention gate. This mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-access.ts`, which already uses `hasControlCommand` for the group activation path and reserves `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` for DMs.

The group/DM split is a small `resolveLineControlCommand` helper in `group-policy.ts`, next to `resolveLineGroupRequireMention` (the file's other gating resolver); `bot-handlers.ts` (a size-capped file) calls it and stays within its line cap.

## User Impact

LINE groups with requireMention no longer surface the bot for plain messages that merely contain a `/word` or `!word` token. Real control commands from authorized members still bypass requireMention, @mentions still work, and DM behavior is unchanged. No privilege change — command execution was, and still is, gated by CommandAuthorized.

## Evidence

Two review follow-ups from the previous round are folded in here:

- **[P2] positive regression now exercises a real registered command.** The bypass case previously sent `!status`, which the mocked command-auth module treated as a control command via a naive `startsWith("!")`. Production `hasControlCommand` matches the body against **registered command aliases** (e.g. `/status`, `acceptsArgs`), so `!status` is only an inline token — the test could pass without proving that a genuine control command still bypasses `requireMention`. The bypass cases now send the registered `/status` alias, and the mock reflects the real split: `hasControlCommand` = "starts with a registered alias" (precise); `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` = the real `hasInlineCommandTokens` regex over `/x`/`!x` (broad). The two detectors are now genuinely distinguishable, so the group precise-detector path is actually exercised.
- **[P1] real LINE group behavior proof** added below (redacted inbound gating trace).

### Red↔green — the fix's own test

Reverting **only** the group/DM split (the helper falls back to the broad detector) makes the guard test fail, because the plain `cd /home` message now reaches the agent:

```
 × does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
      Tests  1 failed | 29 passed (30)
```

With the fix applied, the guard passes and its companion stays green — a real `/status` from an allowlisted member still bypasses `requireMention`, so the fix narrows over-activation without breaking legitimate command bypass:

```
 ✓ does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 ✓ still bypasses requireMention for an allowlisted real control command
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### Behavior (group `requireMention: true`, sender in `groupAllowFrom`, no @mention)

| message | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cd /home` (plain, inline "/" token) | `processMessage` called — dispatched to agent ❌ | skipped ✓ |
| `/status` (registered control command) | dispatched ✓ | dispatched ✓ |

### Real LINE group — inbound gating trace (redacted)

Fixed branch running against a real LINE Messaging API webhook, in a real group with `requireMention: true` and the sender in `groupAllowFrom` (no @mention in either message). Group/user identifiers, message/session ids, and the display name are redacted.

Plain message with an inline "/" token — **not** bypassed, skipped before any agent dispatch:

```
line: received 1 webhook events
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=line accountId=default peer=group:GROUP_ID guildId=none teamId=none bindings=0
line: skipping group message (requireMention, not mentioned)
```

Registered `/status` control command from the same allowlisted member — bypasses `requireMention` and is handed to the agent handler:

```
line inbound: from=line:group:GROUP_ID len=119 preview="[LINE group:GROUP_ID …] USER_ID: /status"
line: received message from [member] (line:group:GROUP_ID)
```

`line: received message from …` prints only after the message clears the `requireMention` gate into the handler; the plain `cd /home` above never reaches it (it stops at `skipping … requireMention`). This is exactly the precise-vs-broad distinction the patch introduces, confirmed on real inbound traffic.

### Full `bot-handlers.test.ts` suite (vitest)

```
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### Static checks

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts
  Tests  30 passed (30)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test     → exit 0   (test typecheck, no errors)
$ pnpm lint:extensions          → exit 0   (oxlint, no problems)
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts
  All matched files use the correct format.
```

This round touches only `bot-handlers.test.ts`; the production change (`bot-handlers.ts` net 0, `group-policy.ts` helper) is unchanged from the prior push, so the prod typecheck and the LOC ratchet remain green. All output above is real terminal / real-LINE output with identifiers redacted.
